texts.preamble: Master Keerthi Sagar N vs Smt.Bhagyamma on 2 April, 2019 In The Court Of Iii Addl.Judge And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru. (Scch-18) Dated: This 2nd day of April 2019 Present: Sri.Mahantesh S.Dargad B.Sc., LL.B.,(Spl) Iii Addl. Judge & Member, Mact Court Of Small Causes, Bengaluru. M.V.C.No.2723/2017 Petitioner Master Keerthi Sagar N., Son of P.M. Nagaraj, Aged about 15 years, Residing at No.86, Ganesha Temple road, Yerappa Layout, Parappana Agrahara, Bengaluru -100. Since the petitioner being minor Represented by his father and natural guardian Shri P.M.Nagaraj. (By Pleader Shri B.S.Manjunath) V/s Respondents 1. Smt.Bhagyamma, Wife of Shivappa, Residing at No.18/40, Ii main, 5th cross, Ibblur, 2 Scch-18 Mvc 2723/2017 Agara Post, Sarjapura Main Road, Bengaluru-102. (R.C. Owner of HGB/tanker bearing No.KA-51-B-9179) (Exparte) 2. The Reliance General Insurance Company Limited, No.28, East wing, 5th floor, Centenary Building, Master Keerthi Sagar N vs Smt.Bhagyamma on 2 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161347267/ 1 M.G. Road, Bengaluru-560 001. (I.P. No.1409262334001086 valid from 11.6.2016 to 10.6.2017) (By Pleader Shri V.Srihari Naidu) J U D G M E N T
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the petition are as under: On 16.12.2016 at about 6.15 a.m. the petitioner was riding a motor cycle bearing No. KA-51-EC-6582 from his friend house at Sarjapura road, Haralur cross towards Haralur village to attend RSS class slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road, when he reached near O Zone apartment, at that time the driver of the HGV Tanker bearing No.KA-51-9179 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety of others and dashed against the motor cycle. Due to the impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body. Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Sakra hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she was admitted as an inpatient. 3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy, aged about 15 years, studying in 8th standard. On account of the injuries she is permanently disabled and she lost happiness, physically and mentally. The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the HGV lorry. Therefore, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation. Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost. 4. In response to the petition notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court and placed exparte. The respondent No.2 has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed its respective written statement. 5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under: The respondent in its written statement averred that, the claim petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts. Further contended that accident has not occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the Tanker. Further admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-51-B-9179 and its validity. Further contended that the petitioner has filed complaint more than 8 days after the said accident with an intention to fasten the said liability against the respondent insurance company. Further contended that Master Keerthi Sagar N vs Smt.Bhagyamma on 2 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161347267/ 2 neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied mandatory provisions u/s 134 and S.158 (6) of the MV Act. Further denied the age avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition. Contending the above facts, prays to dismiss the claim petition with cost. 6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed: 1. 7. In order to prove the case, the father of the petitioner has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P13 and Medical Record Technician is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P14 to Ex.P17, neuro surgeon is examined as PW3 and got marked the documents at Ex..P18 & Ex. P19 and one witness is examined as PW4 and got marked the document at Ex.P20. 8. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent has examined Senior Medical Record Keeper is examined as RW1 and got marked the document at Ex.R1 & Ex.R2.
texts.arguments: Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had valid and effective driving licence to drive the above said vehicle as on the date of accident, on the other hand, the owner of the motor cycle has willfully entrusted the vehicle to a person who did not had a valid and effective driving licence to drive the tanker on the date of accident. During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner argued by reiterating the contents of petition and also evidence put forth by PW1 to PW4. Further he argued that, the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and Master Keerthi Sagar N vs Smt.Bhagyamma on 2 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161347267/ 3 documentary evidence. Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition. 12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued by denying the manner of the accident as alleged in the petition and contended that accident has not occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the tanker, on the other hand, the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-51-EC-6582 as there were three minor children were proceeding on a motor cycle without wearing helmet. Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondent No.2. 13. 14. In order to prove the case, the father of the petitioner has examined as P.W.1 and he has stated in his evidence by reiterating the contents of petition. The counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued that the petitioner has filed complaint after lapse of 8 days of the incident. 18. Further argued that the offending vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and the said accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle along with two pillion riders without wearing helmet. So, the rider of the motor cycle i.e., the petitioner has also contributed for cause of accident. 19. The respondent No.2 has examined Senior Medical Record Keeper of Sakra Hospital as RW1. He has produced the documents marked at Ex.R1 & Ex.R2, such as authorization letter and true copy of MLC register. He has stated in his evidence that in Ex.R2 not mentioned the number of the vehicle. 20. On the other hand the counsel for the petitioner has argued that motor cyclist may be minor and may not be having a licence cannot be held to be negligent or contributory negligent. In this behalf Master Keerthi Sagar N vs Smt.Bhagyamma on 2 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161347267/ 4 he has relied the decision reported in 1)2018 ACJ 982 in case of Shaktisinh Zala Vs. Zala Ranvirsinh Ranubha and others and another 2) 2016 ACJ 38 in case of Branch Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Biresh Giri and others 3)2010 ACJ 1466 in case of Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Amit Kumar and Others 21. On perusal of the said decisions it is observed that "motor cyclist may be minor and may not be having a licence cannot be held to be negligent or contributory negligent". 22. Hence, I hold that the petitioner has proved his case through oral and documentary evidence. 23. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others). At this juncture this court has relied the decision reported in 2013 ACJ 2445 in between Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co.Ltd.,and another, which reads like thus; Quantum - Injury - Principles of assessment - Assessment of compensation in case of children suffering disability - Apex Court observed that appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc., should be, if the disability is above 10 per cent and up to 30 per cent to the whole body, Rs.3,00,000; up to 60 percent, Rs.4,00,000; up to 90 per cent, Rs.5,00,000 and above 90 per cent, it should be Rs.6,00,000; for permanent disability up to 10 per cent, it should be Rs.1,00,000, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take a different yardstick. 37.
